newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC wants new probe into Hani killing.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC wants new probe into Hani killing.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress called on Friday for a reopening of the investigation into the killing of Communist Party leader Chris Hani four years ago.

Prompted by a newspaper article alleging the state and some ANC security personnel had advance knowledge of the plot to kill Hani, the ANC said the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up to probe apartheid atrocities, should investigate the claims.
Hani was also a member of ANC's executive committee when he was assassinated on April 10, 1993 by two whites -- Conservative Party politician Clive Derby-Lewis and Polish immigrant Janusz Waluz.
Both men, who are serving life sentences for the killing, are now seeking amnesty from the truth commission, led by Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu. No date for the hearing has been announced yet.

"The ANC has always believed that Janusz Waluz and Clive Derby-Lewis could not have acted in isolation but were part of a broader conspiracy to weaken the ANC and its allies before the April 1994 election," ANC spokesman Ronnie Mamoepa told Reuters.
"We are of the view...there exists reasonable grounds for the reopening of investigations into the murder of Chris Hani."

The Weekly Mail and Guardian newspaper reported on Friday the girlfriend of a former Military Intelligence operative, Julie Wilken, had typed up secret reports for him to give to his handlers which warned of Hani's impending assassination.
The reports also claimed that an unidentified group of ANC operatives had conspired with Hani's killers. Wilken's boyfriend died of a single gunshot wound to his head in January 1994.
Mamoepa said the ANC wanted answers to Hani's killing, adding: "The ANC maintains that where crime has been committed the due process of the law must take its course."
The ANC swept into power in 1994 after winning nearly two-thirds of the vote in the country's first all-race election.
